name: Deep Survey

text: A stone plinth with nothing on it, and a card in a brass frame:
PROJECT ABYSS CROWN. RESTRAINT ARRAY, TEST GEOMETRY, ONE TWELFTH SCALE.
The plinth is the size of a table. What goes on it is a mile long.
The far side of the plinth carries the sequence, in four steps.
FIND. WAKE. RING. HOLD. Each step is ticked but the last.
Under WAKE, in a smaller hand: REQUIRES THE HEART. NO SUBSTITUTE FOUND.
One of the twelve. An Aurelian ring, cut out of a temple floor,
and re-wound with new copper and a new throat of glass.
The Aurelians built it to speak with. It has been rebuilt to hold.
A ring that failed testing, kept for comparison, split from rim to hub.
The report card is short. INPUT SUSTAINED 41 SECONDS.
SUBJECT RESPONSE: DISTRESS. TERMINATED ON SAFETY.
A generator the size of a cart, and eleven more like it along the wall.
Twelve rings, twelve generators, and a load sheet that comes to more
current than the city of Aureline draws on a winter night.
A survey mast, dismantled and laid out on trestles with its parts numbered.
It is the same mast the Foundation stands in villages to read the wind.
The instrument at the top of this one is not a wind instrument.
A bench of Aurelian fragments in numbered trays, and a lamp over it.
The work is beautiful. Careful, slow, reversible, properly recorded.
The people who did it were taught by somebody very good.
The deep chart, drawn at last year's soundings and hung under glass.
The shape on the shelf floor is outlined in red and given a bearing,
a depth, and a name that is not a place name.
Crates stencilled for the coast, waybilled to a harbour with no road.
The manifest says SURVEY EQUIPMENT.
The weights on the waybill say twelve of the same thing.
A pallet of coats, boots and cold-weather kit for forty people,
shrink-wrapped and dated for the end of the month.
Whatever this is, it is not a plan. It is a sailing date.
A console still lit, cycling one recorded trace over and over.
It is a pressure reading, taken at depth, and it is not weather.
It rises and falls, slowly, evenly, like something enormous breathing.
The floor plan of this level, and the door out of it at the bottom.
The room beyond is marked ASSEMBLY, and under that, in the same ink
as everything else down here, is written simply: WHEN IT IS TIME.

_plan: The horror is the craftsmanship. This is not a lair: it is a well-run laboratory with tidy trays, honest test reports and a failure kept for comparison, and it happens to be building a cage for something the size of a valley. The twelve rings stand round an empty plinth because what belongs in the middle cannot be brought here. Everything the brief asks Act 4 to deliver about Abyss Crown is on the two plinth cards: FIND, WAKE, RING, HOLD, and REQUIRES THE HEART. The player reads that BEFORE anybody takes the Tideheart off them, which is what makes the theft land.
